commands.name: /continue
commands.result: The next permitted step runs with the same objective, scope and constraints.
commands.needs: Unambiguous current objective and next step.

commands.name: /execute <plan>
commands.intent: Execute a selected plan or tranche
commands.result: The referenced plan is carried through its stated acceptance checks.
commands.needs: Plan version, selected items, bounds and existing approvals.
commands.namingNote: The current session-phases schema uses /run for app launching; /execute is a candidate pending per-provider collision checks.

commands.name: /finish
commands.intent: Carry the current objective to completion
commands.result: Remaining authorized work is advanced to an evidence-backed terminal disposition.
commands.needs: Acceptance predicate and finite runway; no implicit new authority.
examples: walk this all the way home

commands.name: /status
commands.result: Completed, remaining, blocked and unverified work are distinguished.
commands.needs: Current receipts; a denominator for percentages.

commands.name: /next [--owner human]
commands.result: Names the next workstream step or the specific action only the operator can take.
examples: what do i have to do now

commands.name: /explain [--brief|--why]
commands.intent: Clarify the current result or decision
commands.result: A direct explanation at the requested level, without starting a new task.

commands.name: /review <target>
commands.intent: Evaluate an artifact, plan or other session's claims
commands.result: Findings and a reasoned disposition grounded in current evidence.
commands.needs: Target and criteria; imported claims are not proof.
examples: anything you would change or add?

commands.name: /verify <claim>
commands.intent: Check whether the intended result is true
commands.result: A passing or failing predicate with evidence and scope.
commands.needs: The claim and its owning predicate.
examples: were all of the findings healed and addressed?

commands.name: /repair <finding>
commands.result: Cause addressed and the implicated check rerun.
commands.needs: A named failure, authority, and changed-input rule for retries.

commands.name: /revise <delta>
commands.intent: Change the objective, constraint or interpretation
commands.result: The working contract is updated with the explicit new content.
commands.needs: The correction itself cannot be inferred or erased.
examples: the nine phases was me miss counting
do you understand that this is victoroff only right?

commands.name: /approve <proposal-id>
commands.result: An exact prepared proposal receives approval while exclusions remain intact.
commands.needs: Proposal identity/version, target, scope, conditions, expiration if relevant.
examples: yes to 1 and 2, wait on copilot

commands.name: /ship <stage> <target>
commands.result: Push, PR, merge or deploy succeeds with stage-specific evidence.
commands.needs: Explicit stage and target. Merge, deployment and cleanup stay separate.

commands.name: /closeout
commands.result: Work has durable owners, required receipts and the session-release predicate.
commands.needs: Current obligations and source-owned closeout implementation.

commands.name: /archive-check
commands.intent: Check whether a session can be archived
commands.result: A reasoned eligible/ineligible verdict; no archive mutation.
commands.needs: Custody, outstanding ownership and session identity.
examples: safe to archive this work session?

commands.name: /context <payload>
commands.result: Payload is retained with its source and interpreted against the active objective.
commands.needs: The actual output, transcript, attachment or document.

commands.name: /handoff <scope> <target>
commands.intent: Prepare or send a bounded continuation
commands.result: Scope, authority, evidence and next action travel together.
commands.needs: Recipient and explicit send instruction; preparation alone sends nothing.
examples: provide a handoff prompt for each

commands.name: /reorient
commands.intent: Correct a stalled or drifting approach
commands.result: Compare work against the original objective, identify the loop or mismatch, and choose a materially different authorized next action.
commands.needs: Evidence of no progress or scope drift; preserve the objective and hard limits.
examples: you are spiralling on the same things over and over
you should be following a plan
